text: The subject, Talha Nawaz, a low‑risk senior manager earning PKR 600,000 per month, opened his account in December 2023. Within a three‑week period (2 Mar – 23 Mar 2026) the account received a series of large cash deposits at the Clifton branch that total PKR 9,896,300, each ranging from PKR 276,000 to PKR 1,001,000. Several deposits (e.g., PKR 1,001,000 on 23 Mar, PKR 1,852,000 on 9 Mar, PKR 1,682,000 on 17 Mar) are at or just below the typical cash‑transaction reporting (CTR) threshold of PKR 1 million, a pattern flagged by the typology engine (rule 045) as “Repeated cash deposits within 20% below the CTR threshold.” The deposits were made across the same branch in rapid succession (rule 046), indicating possible structuring to avoid reporting. Moreover, the subject’s declared monthly income (PKR 600,000) cannot plausibly support such inflows, and there is no business justification for the cash, as the only inbound electronic transfer was a single salary payment of PKR 600,000 from his employer. The subsequent outbound IBFT of PKR 2,807,000 to Crescent Imports on 5 Mar further suggests the cash is being used to fund a large payment. These factors collectively warrant filing a Suspicious Transaction Report.
